facts.claim: People in a cold state systematically underpredict how strongly a later hot state will change desire and behavior.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because current visceral conditions are difficult to simulate, so calm forecasts discount hunger, craving, pain, or arousal.
facts.commonError: Knowing that temptation exists is enough to forecast its strength accurately.
facts.whyWrong: Awareness of a future state does not reproduce its motivational force.

facts.claim: Removing the cashews made dinner guests better off by their own expressed judgment despite reducing their immediate option set.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because the removed temptation protected their prior plan to preserve appetite for dinner.
facts.commonError: An additional available option can never make a chooser worse off.
facts.whyWrong: A tempting option changes behavior when present preferences conflict with advance preferences.

facts.claim: Christmas Club accounts traded interest and liquidity for a withdrawal restriction tied to holiday spending.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because earmarking and delayed access prevented the Doer from spending savings before the intended date.
facts.commonError: A lower-return restricted account has no rational value to its depositor.
facts.whyWrong: The constraint supplies self-control that an unrestricted account does not.

facts.claim: Dynamic inconsistency occurs when a person's preferred action changes as the moment of temptation approaches.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because immediate rewards gain disproportionate weight at short delays, so a plan made earlier can reverse later.
facts.commonError: A changed choice necessarily proves the earlier preference was insincere.
facts.whyWrong: Both preferences can be genuine but activated at different times.

facts.claim: A commitment device works by changing the future choice set or its consequences before temptation arrives.
facts.mechanism: Advance action transfers control to the calm planning state so that later impulse cannot act as freely.
facts.commonError: Commitment devices merely provide motivational slogans.
facts.whyWrong: Their defining feature is a concrete constraint, stake, or barrier.

facts.claim: Mental accounting assigns nominally interchangeable dollars to separate purposes such as rent, leisure, or emergencies.
facts.mechanism: Labels create internal spending boundaries so that using one account feels different from using another.
facts.commonError: People naturally treat every dollar as perfectly fungible in practice.
facts.whyWrong: Household budgets and earmarked accounts display persistent category boundaries.

facts.claim: The Planner represents long-horizon welfare while the Doer gives heavier weight to immediate gratification.
facts.mechanism: The two-self model separates advance evaluation from state-dependent action so that self-control conflict becomes analyzable.
facts.commonError: Planner and Doer refer to two anatomical brain regions with fixed control.
facts.whyWrong: They are an economic model of competing time horizons, not a literal map of two organs.

facts.claim: Large containers and portions can increase consumption when eating proceeds with little attention.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because external cues substitute for an internal stopping rule, so quantity served influences quantity consumed.
facts.commonError: Portion size affects only people who consciously decide to finish everything.
facts.whyWrong: The proposed mechanism is mindless cue-following rather than an explicit clean-plate rule.

facts.claim: Ulysses' mast strategy is a commitment device because the restraint is chosen before the Sirens can alter his behavior.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because binding future action while calm prevents the later hot state from executing its preferred course.
facts.commonError: The story illustrates stronger willpower at the moment of temptation.
facts.whyWrong: The solution removes reliance on momentary willpower by imposing an earlier constraint.

allowedAnchors.text: One set of preferences favors future welfare while another responds strongly to immediate rewards and arousal. A decision that seems inconsistent can be understood and improved by moving control to the earlier planning moment.
